st: Why thinking less about the future is sometimes good for you

sec.t: ff.44.1 The modern fallacy of time in boxes
sec.p: 4000 Weeks opens with a historical excursus. In the Middle Ages, when time couldn't be measured, all human activities were dictated by natural rhythms. There was no point trying to optimise the apple harvest (maybe with KPIs or market analysis): you had to wait for them to…
Even if these boxes existed, how could we ever fill finite boxes with the infinite objects (and experiences) around us?
Decided? Not by chance, in Italian decidere (to decide) shares its root with uccidere (to kill) and recidere (to cut off). Cutting. Removing opportunities.

sec.t: ff.44.4 Wasting 3 hours in front of a painting
sec.p: One of the book's messages is that the constant search for new stimuli and time optimisation is a way to escape the anxiety of standing still. It's a way not to think about our essence, our finitude, our mortality.
